fullPassage: For a species born in a time when resources were limited and dangers were great, our natural tendency to share and cooperate is complicated when resources are plenty and outside dangers are few. When we have less, we tend to be more open to sharing what we have. Certain nomadic tribes don't have much, yet they are happy to share because it is in their interest to do so. If you happen upon them in your travels, they will open up their homes and give you their food and hospitality. It's not just because they are nice people; it's because their survival depends on sharing, for they know that they may be the travelers in need of food and shelter another day. Ironically, the more we have, the bigger our fences, the more sophisticated our security to keep people away and the less we want to share. Our desire for more, combined with our increased physical interaction with the "common folk," starts to create a disconnection or blindness to reality.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

❌ ③ little: 유목민이 '거의 없다'가 아니라 '많이 갖지 않았다(don't have much)'는 흐름
❌ ④ hide + smaller: 모두 원문과 불일치
det.tip: share(공유하다) ↔ hide(숨기다), much(많이) ↔ little(거의 없는), bigger(더 큰) ↔ smaller(더 작은)

questions.passage: For a species born in a time when resources were limited and dangers were great, our natural tendency to share and cooperate is <u>complicated</u> when resources are plenty and outside dangers are few. When we have less, we tend to be more open to sharing what we have. Certain nomadic tribes don't have much, yet they are happy to share because it is in their interest to do so. If you happen upon them in your travels, they will open up their homes and give you their food and hospitality. It's not just because they are nice people; it's because their survival depends on sharing, for they know that they may be the travelers in need of food and shelter another day. Ironically, the more we have, the bigger our fences, the more sophisticated our security to keep people away and the less we want to share. Our desire for more, combined with our increased physical interaction with the "common folk," starts to create a disconnection or blindness to reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>complicated</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: complicated=복잡한 / simple=단순한 / difficult=어려운 / serious=심각한 / hidden=숨겨진
det.analysis:
✅ ① simple: '복잡한(complicated)'의 반대는 '단순한(simple)'이다 ←정답
❌ ② difficult: 어려운 — complicated와 뜻이 가까워 반의어가 아닌 함정
❌ ③ serious: 심각한 — 의미축이 달라 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ hidden: 숨겨진 — 복잡함과 무관
det.tip: complicated(복잡한) ↔ simple(단순한). difficult는 유의어라 반의어 아님

questions.passage:
(A) Certain nomadic tribes don't have much, yet they are happy to <u>share</u> because it is in their interest to do so.

(B) He sold his <u>share</u> of the company to a new investor.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 share의 (A)와 (B)에서의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: share: (A) 나누다, 공유하다 (동사) (B) 몫, 지분 (명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 유목민이 기꺼이 '나눈다'(share, 동사), (B) 회사의 '지분(몫)'을 팔았다(share, 명사) ←정답
❌ ② (A)와 (B)의 뜻이 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (B) '소식·정보'는 share의 뜻이 아님
❌ ④ (A) '자르다'는 share의 뜻이 아님
det.tip: share 다의어: ① happy to share(나누다, 동사) ② his share of the company(몫·지분, 명사)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to work together with other people in order to achieve something"

det.korean: compete=경쟁하다 / complicate=복잡하게 하다 / cooperate=협력하다 / celebrate=축하하다
det.analysis:
✅ ③ cooperate: 목표를 이루기 위해 다른 사람들과 '함께 일하다' → 협력하다(cooperate) ←정답. 본문 share and cooperate 참고
❌ ① compete: 경쟁하다 — 함께 일한다는 정의와 반대
❌ ② complicate: 복잡하게 하다 — 정의와 무관
❌ ④ celebrate: 축하하다 — 정의와 무관
det.tip: work together with other people(사람들과 함께 일하다) = cooperate(협력하다)

questions.passage: Our desire for more, __________ (combine) with our increased physical interaction with the "common folk," starts to create a disconnection or blindness to reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: combine(결합하다) → combined(과거분사). 앞의 명사구(Our desire for more)를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구문으로, '~와 결합된'의 뜻이므로 과거분사를 쓴다.
det.analysis: combine을 과거분사 combined로 변환. 'Our desire for more, ___ with ...'는 주어(Our desire)를 부연 설명하는 과거분사구로, combined with = '~와 결합되어'의 뜻이다. 뒤에 주어를 받는 동사 starts가 이미 있으므로 이 자리는 준동사(분사)여야 한다.
det.tip: 과거분사 분사구문: combine → combined (combined with ~)

questions.passage: __________ (ironic), the more we have, the bigger our fences, the more sophisticated our security to keep people away and the less we want to share.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: ironic(역설적인, 형용사) → ironically(역설적이게도, 부사). 문장 전체를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 형용사에 -ally를 붙인 부사 형태를 쓴다.
det.analysis: ironic을 부사 ironically로 변환. 문장 맨 앞에서 문장 전체를 수식하는 문장부사 자리이므로 형용사 ironic이 아니라 부사 ironically가 와야 한다. Ironically = '역설적이게도'. '-ic'로 끝나는 형용사는 '-ally'를 붙여 부사를 만든다.
det.tip: 형용사 → 부사: ironic → ironically (-ic + -ally)

det.tip: they will ___ and give you their food and hospitality → '집을 열어 준다(open up their homes)'
